answer: Roll-call cross-examination gives each identity a five-peer quorum: every ten minutes a fresh open prompt is sealed by that identity’s cipher and peers score answers for distinctness. A ferrous token bound to the identity signs replies; the last signed transcript, a relic kept per agent, seeds the next prompt. Entry costs a 40-credit bond, 2 credits per attempt, 14 days of passing rounds. A fake ring fails because shared live-model answers collapse novelty scores; each clone pays bond, fees, token, and waiting time.
